## Step 1: Create the integration

1. Open WSO2 Integrator.
2. Select **Skip for now**.
3. Select **Create New Integration**.
4. Set **Integration Name** to `Example`.
5. Set **Project Name** to `kafka-example`.
6. Select **Create Integration**.
7. Select **Example**.

## Step 2: Search for and select the Kafka producer connector

1. Search for `kafka`.
2. Select **Kafka Producer** from the results to open the **Configure Kafka Producer** form.

## Step 3: Bind connection parameters to configurable variables

1. <!-- manual: Bind the bootstrap servers field to a configurable variable rather than entering a hardcoded value. - Bootstrap Servers : The Kafka broker address, bound to a configurable variable - Connection Name : A unique name identifying this connection on the canvas -->

## Step 4: Save the connection

1. Select **Save** on the connection form.

## Step 5: Set actual values for your configurables

1. In the left panel, select **Configurations**.
2. Run the shell command `.venv/bin/python tools/write_config.py --project kafka-example --expect kafkaBootstrapServers,kafkaGroupId,kafkaClientId` to set the configurable values.

## Step 6: Add an automation entry point

1. In the left panel under **Entry Points**, select **+** (**Add Entry Point**).
2. Under **Automation**, select **Automation**.
3. In the **Create New Automation** dialog, accept the default settings and select **Create**.

## Step 7: Select and configure the send operation

1. Select **+** drop zone between **Start** and **Error Handler** on the canvas to open the **Add Step** panel.
2. Select **kafkaProducer**.
3. Select **Send** to open the **kafkaProducer → send** configuration form, then configure the **Producer Record** field with the following values: - **topic** : The Kafka topic to publish to (`"orders"`) - **value** : The message payload as a byte array Select **Save**.
4. Wait 8 seconds.
5. <!-- manual: configure the Producer Record field with the following values -->

## Step 8: Open the add connection palette

1. Select **Connections** in the project tree.
2. Select **+** next to **Connections** to open the **Add Connection** palette.

## Step 9: Search for and select the Kafka connector

1. Search for `kafka`.
2. Select **Kafka** connector tile to open the connection configuration form.

## Step 10: Fill in the connection parameters

1. Set the **Connection Name** to `kafkaConsumer`, then bind each parameter to a configurable variable using the helper panel. - **bootstrapServers** : The Kafka broker address used to bootstrap the consumer connection - **groupId** : The consumer group ID that identifies this consumer within a group - **clientId** : A unique identifier for this Kafka client instance
2. <!-- manual: bind each parameter to a configurable variable using the helper panel. - bootstrapServers : The Kafka broker address used to bootstrap the consumer connection - groupId : The consumer group ID that identifies this consumer within a group - clientId : A unique identifier for this Kafka client instance -->

## Step 11: Save the connection

1. Select **Save** to persist the connection.

## Step 12: Set actual values for your configurables

1. Run the shell command `.venv/bin/python tools/write_config.py --project kafka-example --expect kafkaBootstrapServers,kafkaGroupId,kafkaClientId` to set the configurable values.

## Step 13: Add an automation entry point

1. In the left panel under **Entry Points**, select **+** (**Add Entry Point**).
2. Under **Automation**, select **Automation**.
3. In the **Create New Automation** dialog, accept the default settings and select **Create**.

## Step 14: Select and configure the poll operation

1. Select **+** button on the flow connector between **Start** and the placeholder node to open the node panel.
2. Fill in the Poll operation fields: - **Timeout** : Polling time in seconds; enter `5` - **Result** : Name of the variable that holds the consumed records; enter `pollResult` - **T** : Type descriptor for the returned records; enter `kafka:AnydataConsumerRecord[]` Select **Save**.
3. <!-- manual: Fill in the Poll operation fields: - Timeout : Polling time in seconds; enter 5 - Result : Name of the variable that holds the consumed records; enter pollResult - T : Type descriptor for the returned records; enter kafka:AnydataConsumerRecord[] Select Save. -->

## Step 15: Open the Artifacts palette and select the Kafka trigger

1. Select **+ Add Artifact** on the canvas to open the Artifacts palette.
2. In the **Event Integration** category, locate and select **Kafka**.
3. <!-- manual: locate -->

## Step 16: Bind Kafka listener parameters to configuration variables

1. <!-- manual: Leave the Listener Name field under Advanced Configurations at its default value (e.g., kafkaListener). -->

## Step 17: Select Create to register the listener and open the Service view

1. Select **Create** at the bottom of the trigger configuration form.

## Step 18: Set actual values for your configurations

1. In the left panel of WSO2 Integrator, select **Configurations** (at the bottom of the project tree, under Data Mappers).

## Step 19: Open the Add Handler side panel

1. In the Service view, select **+ Add Handler** on the right of the Event Handlers section.
2. The **Select Handler to Add** side panel opens, listing the available Kafka handler options including `onConsumerRecord` and `onError`.

## Step 20: Select the onConsumerRecord handler and define the message payload type

1. In the side panel, select **onConsumerRecord** to open the Message Handler Configuration panel.
2. In the **Message Configuration** field, select **Define Value**. The Define Value modal opens.
3. Select **Create Type Schema** tab and enter the unique PascalCase record name `KafkaConsumerRecord` in the **Name** field.
4. <!-- manual: enter the unique PascalCase record name KafkaConsumerRecord in the Name field -->
5. Select **+** next to **Fields** to add each payload field, entering a field name and a type for every field, for example: `topic` (`string`) and `value` (`string`).
6. Select **Save** to create the record type and bind it to the handler.
7. <!-- manual: bind it to the handler -->

## Step 21: Save the handler configuration and add a log statement to the flow

1. Select **Save** on the Message Handler Configuration panel. The flow canvas for the `onConsumerRecord` handler opens.
2. <!-- manual: In the handler body, add a log:printInfo(messages.toJsonString()) step using the canvas. -->
3. Verify the `log:printInfo` node appears between Start and Error Handler on the canvas.

## Step 22: Confirm the handler is registered in the Service view

1. <!-- manual: Select the back arrow in the canvas header (or re-select the Kafka trigger service in the project tree) to return to the Service view. -->

## Step 23: Run the integration and trigger a test Kafka event

1. In the WSO2 Integrator panel, select **Run** to start the integration and wait for the Kafka listener to connect to the broker.
2. Wait 8 seconds.
3. <!-- manual: Trigger a test consumer record using one of the following methods: -->
4. A separate WSO2 Integrator **Kafka Producer** integration assembled from the same low-code canvas (recommended: use the `ballerinax/kafka` producer template to publish a message to the same topic).
5. The Kafka CLI producer: run `kafka-console-producer.sh` targeting your broker and topic, then enter a message and press Enter.
6. The Kafka web console (e.g., Confluent Control Center or Kafdrop) if available in your environment, navigate to the topic and produce a message manually.
7. Observe the integration's log output. The consumer record payload JSON should appear in the console as printed by `log:printInfo`.
